- Identifiers and naming (Sec 3.1): Use clear, scoped names (e.g., branding::kBrandName) and avoid global mutable state.
- Character encoding (Sec 2.4): Ensure UTF‑8 handling end‑to‑end to prevent mojibake in UI/logs.
- I18N/L10N (Sec 8.2): Do not hardcode user‑facing text. Use translation keys and locale resources; only the canonical brand token should be in code.
- Logging and PII (Sec 9.3): Don’t log the brand token in high‑volume paths unless necessary; if logged, keep it at INFO with rate limiting.
- Configuration (Sec 4.4): If this is white‑label capable, make the brand value runtime‑configurable (env/config service), with safe defaults and validation.
- Security (Sec 10.2): No embedded secrets, API tokens, or feature flags alongside branding. Load secrets from the vault/inject via CI. If unsure, escalate to Security Engineering.
- Assets (Sec 11.1): Place logos/fonts in the approved assets pipeline with license metadata and content hashing; avoid loading assets from remote URLs at runtime.
- Testing (Sec 12.1): Add unit tests covering all code paths that reference the brand token (formatting, rendering, fallbacks). Target ≥95% line/branch coverage. Include snapshot/Golden tests for UI where applicable.
